title: Accelerating MILP-Based Differential Cryptanalysis
summary: Cryptographic MILP instances are unusually hard to solve at comparable scale; specialized solvers are needed to extend differential analysis to more cipher rounds.

formal_statement.body: The target is the mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) instances used to evaluate and search differential characteristics in bit-oriented block ciphers. These instances can yield tighter security bounds and characteristics covering more cipher rounds or having larger probabilities, but they are very hard to solve compared with general MILP problems of the same scale in variables and constraints. The unresolved task is to develop specialized optimization methods that accelerate solving these cryptographic MILP instances, thereby enabling analysis of a larger number of cipher rounds.

scope.domain: Automated differential cryptanalysis of bit-oriented block ciphers using mixed-integer linear programming.
parameters: Number of cipher rounds: determines how much of the cipher can be analyzed
Numbers of MILP variables and constraints: measure instance scale for comparison with general MILP problems
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop specialized optimization methods that solve these cryptographic MILP instances faster and enable analysis of more cipher rounds.

citations.label: Automatic Security Evaluation and (Related-key) Differential Characteristic Search: Application to SIMON, PRESENT, LBlock, DES(L) and Other Bit-Oriented Block Ciphers

progress.summary: The paper explicitly identifies the poor scalability of its cryptographic MILP instances as an open problem. It calls for specific acceleration methods so that more cipher rounds can be handled.
